verdicts.title: Payload-wrap idiom duplicated between ol_reset and ol_make_any
verdicts.reasoning: Read any_type.py lines 59-82. ol_reset closure at lines 64-65: `self.p = _cast(_Content(x), ErasedType)` / `self.t = ty_code`. ol_make_any closure at lines 79-80: `any.p = _cast(_Content(x), ErasedType)` / `any.t = ty_code`. Both derive ty_code identically as `str(x_ty)` (lines 61 and 75). The two-line erasure idiom is written verbatim twice. The maintenance hazard is real: a change to the _Content wrapping, cast target type, or type-code derivation must be applied at both sites or the payload and .t tag will disagree, causing ol_get_as to either reject or misdecode the value. This is not a known-correct pattern, not guarded elsewhere, and the severity 'low' is appropriate since it is currently non-buggy.
